summary: The bill makes it a federal crime to knowingly publish nonconsensual intimate images or AI-generated deepfakes of adults or minors on interactive online services, and requires major websites and apps to remove such content within 48 hours after receiving a valid request from the person depicted.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal appropriations, new spending programs, or budget authorizations. Enforcement is assigned to the existing FTC without any funding mandates.
No tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures appear in the bill.
The legislation does not address healthcare delivery, insurance, or medical regulation.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill has no immigration, border, or visa-related content.
No provisions concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
No military, defense, or national security spending language.
The bill does not engage with environmental regulations or climate policy.
No welfare, entitlement, or social services provisions.
No education funding, school policy, or curriculum content.
The bill does not address controlled substances or drug enforcement.

The bill creates new federal criminal offenses for publishing nonconsensual intimate visual depictions and digital forgeries, with penalties of up to 3 years imprisonment, forfeiture, and restitution requirements. This expands criminal liability and enforcement mechanisms in this domain.
No trade, tariff, or international commerce provisions.
No deficit, debt ceiling, or fiscal policy language.
The bill contains no provisions addressing LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No foreign assistance or international aid measures.
The legislation does not address voting access, election administration, or campaign rules.

The bill imposes new regulatory obligations on covered online platforms, including mandatory notice-and-removal processes for intimate imagery within 48 hours and potential FTC enforcement. This constitutes additional oversight of technology companies.
No labor, employment, or union-related provisions.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
